findings.claim: The change raises `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth` from 500 to 5000. This has nothing to do with REQ-2283, and it weakens the protection for untrusted input. A payload nested between 501 and 5000 levels (for example 1000 nested 1-element arrays, `0x91`…`0xC0`) used to be rejected with `MessagePackSerializationException`. It is now accepted. Recursion up to 5000 deep in the formatters gives attackers more room to exhaust the stack (an unrecoverable `StackOverflowException`, i.e. denial of service). The ledger records a 500 depth limit as a deliberate secure-by-default decision.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.UntrustedDataDepthLimitReceipts.UntrustedData_RejectsGraphNestedDeeperThan500. It deserializes 1000 nested arrays as `object` with `UntrustedData`. It passes on base (an exception is thrown) and fails on head (no exception). Also cite ledger L9 (stack depth limit of 500).

findings.claim: A source-declared positional record property such as `record R([property: Key((string)null)] string Name)` loses its BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic. Its DeclaringSyntaxReference is a `ParameterSyntax`, not a `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, so `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` returns null and the diagnostic gets `Location.None`. The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` filter then drops it because `!IsInSource`. Before, the hard cast threw (AD0001), so the error was at least visible. Now a source type with an invalid key gets no error at all, even though it should be reported at the parameter location.

receipt_plan.detail: Run MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer through `compilation.WithAnalyzers` on a C# 9 source with `[MessagePackObject] public record R([property: Key((string)null)] string Name);` (plus an IsExternalInit shim if needed). Assert that the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull descriptor is reported. On head it is silently absent.

findings.claim: `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` filters every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not in a source tree of the compilation. That also drops diagnostics about SOURCE `[MessagePackObject]` types whose offending member is inherited from a metadata base class. Example: `[MessagePackObject] class Derived : Lib.Base`, where `Base` has a public property without `[Key]`. MemberNeedsKey (MsgPack004) is then located on the metadata member, gets a null location and is discarded. The formatter for `Derived` is still generated, so the inherited member silently goes unserialized. Ledger L8 only exempts types that themselves come from metadata, not source types that inherit metadata members. A better fix is to fall back to the derived type's identifier location instead of dropping the diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a library with `public class Base { public int X { get; set; } }` to a MetadataReference. Then run the analyzers on `[MessagePackObject] public class Derived : Base { [Key(0)] public int Y { get; set; } }` referencing it. Assert that a MsgPack004 diagnostic is reported, located on Derived. On head, no diagnostic is reported.
